title: How RNA methylation regulates jasmonic acid biosynthesis and plant aging
content: Post-transcriptional modifications impact all phases of an mRNA's lifespan, including splicing, transport, translation, and decay (Shen et al. 2023). The most prevalent modification of internal mRNA bases (ie not the 5′ or 3′ ends) is N6-methyladenosine, or m6A. This modification, and the complexes that “write” it, are highly conserved among eukaryotes. In Arabidopsis thaliana, the m6A writer complex consists of adenosine methylases A and B (MTA and MTB) together with the accessory proteins FIP37, VIR, and HAKAI (Ruzicka et al. 2017).
